text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
German-born founder of Reuter's News Agency, BARON PAUL JULIUS VON REUTER, was born in 1816. He began his news service by supplying international news by telegraph.

American novelist ERNEST HEMINGWAY was born in 1899. He used war, bullfighting and fishing symbolically in his work to represent honour, dignity and primitivism. His writings include "A Farewell To Arms" (1929), "For Whom The Bell Tolls" (1940) and "The Old Man And The Sea" (1952). He received the
Nobel Prize for Literature in 1954.
Czech-born film director KAREL REISZ was born in 1926. Films included "Saturday Night And Sunday Morning" and "Morgan: A Suitable Case For Treatment".
British doctor, opera and theatre director JONATHON MILLER was born in 1934.
British drummer with "Herman's Hermits" BARRY WHITHAM was born in 1946.

British singer, guitarist and songwriter CAT STEVENS (STEPHEN DEMETRI GEORGIOU) was born in 1947. His first hit was "Matthew And Son" in 1967 and "I'm Gonna get Me A Gun" in the same year. He also wrote songs for other artists such as "The First Cut Is The Deepest". At the end of 1967 he was diagnosed with T.B. and his career seemed over but he recovered and made a successful comeback in 1970. His subsequent hits included "My Lady D'Arbanville", "Peace Train", "Morning Has Broken", "Oh
Very Young", and "Another Saturday Night". He withdrew from the music industry in the late seventies to became a Muslim and now calls himself YUSUF ISLAM.
** EVENTS **
1796 : Scotland's unofficial Poet Laureate, ROBERT BURNS,
died at the age of 37. He died from rheumatic heart disease, which was could have resulted from years of hardship as a tenant farmer.
1798 : NAPOLEON defeated the Mamelukes at the Battle of
the Pyramids.
1904 : The Trans-Siberian railway was completed after 13
years' work.
1954 : Britain, the United States and the World Bank
turned down President Nasser's plea for aid to build the Aswan Dam on the river Nile.
1960 : Sir FRANCIS CHICHESTER arrived in New York on his
solo round-world journey, having crossed the Atlantic in a record-breaking 40 days.
1960 : The widow of former Sri Lankan Prime Minsiter took
over her late husband's job and became the world's first female PM. SOLOMON BANDARANAIKE was murdered and replaced by his wife SIRMAVO.
1969 : "That's one small step for a man, one giant step

for mankind"...those were the words from NEIL ARMSTRONG as he became the first man to walk on the moon. The Moon walk was televised to hundreds of millions of television viewers around the world and has became one of those "where were you when?" events. US astronaut NEIL ARMSTRONG was followed out of the lunar module, the Eagle, by EDWIN ALDRIN. The pair collected rock samples and took many photographs during their two hours on the lunar surface. It was the most hazardous part of the historic Apollo 11 space mission when the module was manoeuvred onto the moon's surface.
1984 : Poland freed 652 political prisoners.
1985 : A sunken Spanish galleon with about 200 million

dollars in gold, silver and jewels was discovered off the coast of Florida. After a 20-year search, former chicken-farmer MEL FISHER, found the wreck of the "Nuestra Senhora de Atocha". The galleon was one of nine sunk by a hurricane in 1622.
1988 : The eight-year Iran-Iraq war was ?nded by Iran's

spiritual leader AYATOLLAH KHOMEINI. He accepted the UN security council resolution 598, which called for a ceasefire. Previously KHOMEINI had vowed to fight on until IRAQ's SADAM HUSSEIN was overthrown. The war cost more than one million lives, another one million were left homeless and the bill topped the 400 billion dollar mark.
1990 : A huge open-air rock concert was held in Berlin to

celebrate the coming down of "the Wall". It was built in 1961 by East Germany to prevent its residents from moving to the West. Those who tried to escape were shot. The dividing barrier came down as a symbol of the unification of Germany. At the rock concert ROGER WATERS from the group 'Pink Floyd' performed "The Wall".
